newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures erase gains to end lower.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures erase gains to end lower.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended lower on Friday on a lack of follow-through buying after an early rally, dealers said.
The lead Nikkei 225 June contract ended 175 points lower at 20,145 after hitting an early high of 20,480 on light volume of 11,685 lots.
Dealers said the market could head lower next week unless the dollar continued to climb against the yen.

The release of poor Japanese unemployment numbers after Thursday's news of an unexpected drop in industrial output in April gave added credence to the market belief that the Bank of Japan would not raise rates any time soon.

But a dealer with a Japanese house said the weak data also indicated that Japan's economy was still faltering and investors might choose to hold back before the impact of a hike in Japan's consumption tax, imposed on April 1, was clearer.
"Some stop-loss buying was triggered above 20,400 and it went up to 20,480. But when there was no follow-through buying, the market came down again," the dealer said.
He said the June Nikkei could head back below the psychological 20,000 level if support around 20,100 gave way.
The June MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 340.7 against its opening 344.0 on volume of 1,326 lots.
